detailed_description:
Hyperrealistic feline fur, natural cat face and paws, miniature tailored clothes, warm gallery key and cool window fill. No human face or hands.
[Shot 1] Sable starts exactly from the actual near-frontal supported stance, gaze slightly camera-left, with both hindpaws on stone and the bench separated behind-right. A small breath moves the velvet. Its eyes notice the camera moving across the salon. Sable shifts weight onto one hindpaw, lifts the other and takes one measured short forward step; the trailing hindpaw lifts, closes the distance and plants beside it into a comfortable supported stance. The body transfers weight with each landing, the tail counterbalances then settles, and both relaxed forepaws remain genuine furry paws. Only after both paws settle does the head make a small final turn to meet the camera, followed by a single natural blink. The lapel-chain stays attached at both ends and responds to gravity as velvet moves; never floats or grows. The camera starts from the actual reference angle, makes a shallow low diagonal arc toward frontal while preserving the complete step, then a small purposeful rise/push ends on a waist-up face-and-chain composition. The bench remains behind the cat and never supports it. Let the final composed look land with live breathing; no pose reset or still-image freeze. Slow controlled performance is intentional, with clear progression rather than a static slideshow. One cat throughout.

Quiet indoor ambience and soft bare-paw contacts at actual landings, faint fabric friction with movement. No speech, dialogue, narration, singing, meows or human vocalizations.
